subject: Plot three independent circles on a 3d plot

messages.author: 822e23234c9146aa
messages.subject: Plot three independent circles on a 3d plot
parts:
Hi all,
I have an input of three [1:360,2] tables that include measurements on the 1:360 polar coordinates with a good example of one of those tables being the image here.
https://www.mathworks.com/help/examples/antenna/win64/xxpolarpattern_helix.png

I would like to print those three "circles" as different planes circles (x,y,z). I wrote last night a small example that works on the rgl library that plots those three circles by converting the polar coordinates to cartesian ones. You can copy paste the below and see what I mean

require("rgls")

degreeToRadian<-function(degree){
  return   (0.01745329252*degree)
}

turnPolarToX<-function(Amplitude,Coordinate){
  return (Amplitude*cos(degreeToRadian(Coordinate)))
}

turnPolarToY<-function(Amplitude,Coordinate){
  return (Amplitude*sin(degreeToRadian(Coordinate)))
}

# first circle
X1<-turnPolarToX(1,1:360)
Y1<-turnPolarToY(1,1:360)
Z1<-rep(0,360)

# second circle
X2<-turnPolarToX(1,1:360)
Y2<-rep(0,360)
Z2<-turnPolarToY(1,1:360)

# third circle
X3<-rep(0,360)
Y3<-turnPolarToX(1,1:360)
Z3<-turnPolarToY(1,1:360)

Min<-min(X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2,X3,Y3,Z3)
Max<-max(X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2,X3,Y3,Z3)
plot3d(X1,Y1,Z1,xlim=c(Min,Max),ylim=c(Min,Max),zlim=c(Min,Max),box=TRUE,axe=FALSE,add=TRUE,col="red",type="l")
plot3d(X2,Y2,Z2,xlim=c(Min,Max),ylim=c(Min,Max),zlim=c(Min,Max),box=TRUE,axe=FALSE,add=TRUE,col="green",type="l")
plot3d(X3,Y3,Z3,xlim=c(Min,Max),ylim=c(Min,Max),zlim=c(Min,Max),box=TRUE,axe=TRUE,add=FALSE,col="blue",type="l")


the problem I have now is that the axes contain cartesian coordinate values that are not understandable by the user. I am going to try tomorrow to write all this code with ggplot2 and I was wondering if you see that there is a nice way (perhaps by including colors for all those three circles based on their numerical value and then adding a color legend). Will I be able to do something like that with Rstudio? Is it also possible with ggplot2 to include a jpeg image on your Figure?

I would like to thank you in advance for your reply
Regards
Alex
